Hardy–Ramanujan asymptotic as stated in the frozen proof; independent finite enumeration
correctness.rationale: The consecutive-marker condition is local in forbidden blocks; zero extension proves sufficiency for each finite word and creates no new marker triple. For span s between the extreme ones, the sorted positive gaps are an arbitrary partition of s, with n−s placements; s=0 handles a single one and the all-zero word is separate. This gives c_n and C(z). In the Hardy–Ramanujan sum c_n−1=Σ_r r p(n−r), the r/√n window has limit kernel u exp(−a u/2), a=π√(2/3). For r≤n/2 the ratio p(n−r)/p(n) is uniformly bounded by a constant times exp(−ar/(2√n)); the remaining contribution is at most n²p(floor(n/2))=o(np(n)). The integral is 4/a², giving the asserted constant, entropy zero and dimension 1/2. Periodic gaps must be equal cyclically, so each q|n contributes exactly q nonzero points in one orbit and the zero point contributes once. The Euler product for ζ then yields the first differences including n=0. Any strictly increasing successive-gap pair occurs at most once; constant-gap supports with an endpoint are also nonrecurrent (use a run of at least q zeros immediately beyond the endpoint, where q is the common marker distance). Poincaré recurrence on a countable cylinder basis therefore puts all invariant measure on the disjoint periodic orbits, with uniquely determined uniform-orbit masses. An independent enumerator matched all finite words through length 16 and cyclic states through length 12, as well as first differences through index 15; the ratios to the leading asymptotic at n=200,400,800 were approximately 0.9955643, 0.9969964, 0.9979437. No frozen script was executed.
residual_risks: Finite enumerations do not prove the asymptotic or recurrence rigidity. The measure conclusion uses ordinary point recurrence and does not assert that all points in the supports of invariant measures are periodic.

value.rationale: This one elementary shift provides an exact comparison between substantial but subexponential word growth and entirely periodic invariant measures. In addition to the growth scale, it gives a sharp asymptotic constant and a coefficient identity tying the periodic zeta function to the full language. The identity is more informative than a proof that systems with entropy dimension 1/2 exist, and the example can be used to separate language growth from the behavior of all invariant measures without a fitted parameter sequence.
residual_risks: The coefficient link is asserted only for this shift; it need not hold for general constrained gap shifts or arbitrary zero-entropy systems.
